panel.introduction: Closest to the Sun, Mercury is the smallest planet: a cratered terrestrial world with a large metallic core and extreme surface temperatures.

controls.label: 750 nm
controls.title: MDIS Global Basemap BDR
controls.filter: MESSENGER MDIS BDR global 750 nm monochrome basemap
controls.summary: Brightness at 750 nm varies with the surface and the lighting when each image was taken. The mosaic is grayscale.

controls.label: Enhanced
controls.description: Enhanced, NASA Trek/USGS MESSENGER enhanced-color mosaic with qualified prepared coverage completion false color Missing polar regions use reconstructed color from nearby enhanced imagery with BDR and topographic detail; these are not observed enhanced-color coverage.
controls.title: MDIS Enhanced Color Mosaic
controls.filter: NASA Trek/USGS MESSENGER enhanced-color mosaic with qualified prepared coverage completion
controls.summary: Colors distinguish surface materials. Missing polar color is reconstructed from nearby imagery and terrain, not observed.

controls.label: Topography
controls.title: MDIS Color Shaded Relief
controls.filter: USGS MESSENGER global color shaded relief
controls.summary: Colors show elevation, while shading makes slopes visible. Both describe the terrain; they do not depict its visible color.

controls.label: Interior
controls.title: Interior structure model
controls.summary: A large metallic core sits inside a rocky outer shell. Layer sizes follow the structural model; colors identify each layer.

source.title: Computing Apparent Planetary Magnitudes for The Astronomical Almanac
